text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Brian Quinn has spent the past two nights behind bars after being found guilty of conspiring to defraud Coles Myer of A$4.5 million in the Victorian Supreme Court on Saturday. Quinn, the former chief executive of the retail giant, is to appeal the decision, but faces a new challenge when the findings of an investigation into a controversial share transaction between Coles and Yannon Pty Ltd - conducted when Quinn was chief executive - are released. Page 1.

Australian Securities Commission chairman Alan Cameron revealed yesterday the Commission's investigation into the Yannon transaction - one of the ASC's most significant cases - is almost complete. The investigation into the 1990 deal which cost Coles Myer A$18 million was passed to the Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions in June last year. Page 5.

According to the half-yearly report of CanWest Global Communications Corp, which controls 76 per cent of the Ten Network, the Australian television broadcaster has recorded revenue growth of about 8 per cent for the half-year to February, with CanWest's share of the revenue sitting at A$158.3 million for the six months. Page 21.

Lanes Ltd, better known for its Mercedes-Benz dealerships and Bristol Paint shops, is to be exposed to competition in its traditional forklift truck monopoly in Melbourne after Toyota announced the Victorian city will soon see a second franchise. Lanes, one of Australia's biggest forklift dealers through its Princetown materials handling subsidiary, has been the sole Toyota dealer in Melbourne for 25 years. Page 21.

Gary Weiss, executive director of Sir Ron Brierley's Guinness Peat Group plc, announced yesterday the brewing giant has increased its stake in cash-box Tooth & Co Ltd to 25 per cent and said GPG would continue to look at lifting its stake under the provisions of the takeover rules. Weiss also indicated the company may play an underwriting role in the upcoming Adsteam Marine float. Page 23.

Speaking on the Nine Network's Business Sunday program yesterday, AMP Society chief executive George Trumbull predicted the company's total assets under management could top the A$100 billion mark by the second half of next year when it lists on the Austrlian Stock Exchange, but warned its earnings could remain volatile. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Wallis report is to come under further criticism today at a conference on the Wallis inquiry into the country's financial system. Today's speech by Peter Smith, the managing director of the Australian Payments Clearing System Association, which is chaired by Reserve Bank deputy governor Graham Thompson, is expected to criticise the report for trying to solve problems that do not exist. Page 17.

The Industrial Relations Commission will release its judgement on the ACTU's living wage claim this week amid market expectations of an inflation-friendly compromise between the ACTU's claim of A$20 a week for workers not covered by an enterprise agreement and an 8.75 per cent boost to the minimum wage, and the Federal Government's offer of A$8 a week. Page 17. --

After suffering cost increases of more than A$100 million at the A$1.35 billion Bajo de la Alumbrera copper and gold joint venture project, venture partners Miners North Ltd and MIM Holdings, which controls 50 per cent of the project, have broadened the regular discussions to include merger negotiations. Page 17.

After a positive report from Government forecaster ABARE that there have been record cotton and canola plantings this year, while sunflower plantings have doubled, Cargill Australia managing director Michael Pallett has announced the company will commission a A$35 million oilseed crushing plant in Newcastle this week. Page 19

In a campaign aimed at promoting the prevention of tax minimisation schemes, rather than prosecution, the Australian Securities Commission has launched a campaign urging potential investors to report any questionable tax minimisation promoters. The move comes as the ASC seeks to promote its consumer protection credentials. Page 19.

Following New South Wales' bumper wheat harvest and a lower cost base, Graincorp, a grain handling company formerly run by the State Government, but privatised in 1992, has cleared its start-up debt and has embarked on a A$45 million capital works program Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

United States billionaire Kirk Kerkorian, who bought Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer with Kerry Stokes' Seven Network for US$1.3 billion in 1996, is negotiating to buy Orion Pictures for A$387 million and merge the company into MGM/UA. Kerkorian currently has a US$700 million investment in MGM/UA. Page 37.

In a move which comes amid much market speculation about the identity of the buyer or buyers of A$100 million-plus of John Fairfax Holdings shares which weren't offered to institutional shareholders, Fairfax is considering forcing the owners of close to five per cent of the newspaper group sold by Conrad Black's Hollinger group to reveal their identity. Page 37.

Access Economics has predicted the 2000 Sydney Olympics could help Australia escape the usual boom-and-bust business cycle. The next global economic slowdown is thought to be due approximately at 2000 but the economic activity associated with the Games is likely to offset the usual effects of a recession in Australia. Access economics further predicted that Australia will experience rapid economic growth over the coming two years. Page 37.

The Australian Securities Commission's (ASC) 18-month investigation into the Coles-Myer-Yannon affair should be concluded quickly and produce an "appropriate outcome' claimed the ASC's chairman Alan Cameron yesterday. The chairman was speaking in response to criticism of the ASC performance as a corporate watchdog. Page 37.

The London financial community is speculating that the AMP Society may be preparing a bid for UK insurance group Norwich Union before its float in June. Last Friday Norwich Union shareholders approved the proposal to transform the life and general insurace group from a mutual to a publicly listed company. Page 39.

The Ten Network has increased its earnings for its principal shareholder, Canadian CanWest Global, by 38 per cent to A$158 million, for the first half of the financial year. The results were released on Friday and are the first indication of the network' performance over the January and February months. Page 39.
THE AGE

The AMP society is preparing to extend its PriorityOne direct banking subsidiary into a serious banking operation. AMP's managing director George Trumball speaking on the Nine Network's Business Sunday, said the application for a banking license would be made very quickly with the new venture being renamed the AMP Bank. Page B1.

The ANZ Bank's latest Investment Monitor reports that residential property remains the most profitable way to invest money. In the three months to March property values across Australia increased by 9.6 per cent, outstripping the returns from shares, fixd interest, cash, gold bullion and superannuation funds. Page B1.

The stock of Oil Search, the PNG specialist explorer company has surged in response to the Moran discovery and the continuing exploration potential of its PNG permits, which are joint ventures with Chevron and BHP Petroleum. Last Friday Oil Search's stock jumped 16 cents to a record of A$3.09 for a total market value of A$1.44 billion. Page B3.

The oil company Novus Petroleum is currently performing very well. Oil Conference week saw its stock close on a record last Friday with A$3.76 a share making for a total market value of A$413 million. Novus Petroleum has utilised both exploration succes and shrewd trading in oil and gas assets to increase its stock value from its original 1995 A$1.50 a share. Page B3.

The Garimpeiro company tried to drum-up Australian investment interest in the Sydney-based Petsec Energy Group at last week's Oil Conference. Thepromotion-drive was in response to the company's sluggish share price over recent months. Petsec Energy is focused on the shallow water potential of the Gulf of Mexico and consequently enjoys strong support in the US. Page B3.

Access Economics has predicted that Victoria's growth rate will lag behind the national average over the next five years. The Melbourne and Canberra based consulting firm has just released its latest five-year forecasts with its which included prediction that the Australian economy will experience two years of rapid growth followed by a wages breakout that will result in a near-recession by 2001. Page B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
